correctness.rationale: In the stated regime, the first selected vertex of an untouched blade footprints another vertex there; the second footprints the first; two already dominate that blade and the center. Hence at most two vertices of each blade are legal, and selecting two in each attains length 2r in any order. Starting at the center yields length at most two. If the center is used after a peripheral vertex, it must be last; it cannot follow two selections in every blade because all vertices are already dominated. This last observation makes explicit the upper bound for sequences containing the center, implicit in RESULT.md lines 59–65. At length 2r with a terminal center, exactly one blade thus contributes one vertex, which itself remains undominated until the center. All permutations of the peripheral prefix work. Counting the two disjoint classes gives M(W) and Q(W), with per-set multipliers (2r)! and (2r−1)!, respectively. The homogeneous specialization follows; for two triangular blades there are five supports and 48 sequences.
residual_risks: The original 33-profile subset-DP replay is supplementary; correctness here rests on the all-parameter proof, not on rerunning that finite check.

value.rationale: The scalar alone cannot tell whether the universal center appears or how its presence changes the number of orders. This natural and fully heterogeneous family admits an exact description and different per-support multiplicities, useful for comparing center participation, counting, or sampling extremizers without enumerating orders. This is a modest complete classification, not a new algorithm for general cographs.
